subject: Post-demo: model fit, benchmarks, next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@saasco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-18T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo notes - model fit, benchmarks, next steps

Hi Alex -

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

- Observations: your use case (support ticket summarization + routing) looks like a good fit for a mid-sized model with strong instruction-following (we saw hallucination sensitivity on some longer context examples).
- Recommended starting models: xwin-7B-fp16 (balanced quality/latency), xwin-3B-quant (lower-cost option for high-throughput).
- Attached: prompt_set_v1.json (your sample prompts converted for eval) and benchmark_summary_20260318.pdf (high-level perf/quality tradeoffs we discussed).
- Next steps: please confirm your target latency (p95) and an acceptable quality threshold (F1/ROUGE/qualitative pass rate). If you can share a few more representative prompts or a small set of ticket examples we can run our eval harness and return a concrete recommendation and an A/B plan.

If you'd like, Rishi can run a quick targeted eval tomorrow and propose a pin/rollback plan in case you want to freeze a previous version.

Thanks -
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198

Attachments: prompt_set_v1.json, benchmark_summary_20260318.pdf

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@saasco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jenny Liu <jenny.liu@saasco.com>
Date: 2026-03-18T18:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo notes - model fit, benchmarks, next steps

Marissa, thanks for the summary and for the attachments - super helpful. A couple quick things from our side: 

- Target latency: p95 <= 220ms for short prompts (<= 256 tokens); longer contexts can be higher.
- Quality threshold: we need at least 92% pass on our internal rubric for routing accuracy.

One important data point: over the last 48 hours we started seeing a spike in incorrect labels after what appears to be a backend model update (we're on the hosted API). Some examples attached (error_log_screenshot.png). Behavior seems consistent with a quality regression vs what we saw last week. Is there an easy way to pin to a prior model version while you investigate diffs?

Happy to schedule a short call if that helps.

- Alex
Head of ML Products, SaaSCo
alex.turner@saasco.com

Attachment: error_log_screenshot.png

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@saasco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-19T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Post-demo notes - model fit, benchmarks, next steps

Hi Alex -

Thanks for flagging this and for the screenshot. Quick technical notes and immediate options: 

1) Pinning: we can pin your routing to a specific model artifact (we recommend pinning to model-xwin-7B@2026-02-14 which matches the behavior you described). Pinning is immediate and can be scoped to a route or API key.

2) Diffs & likely causes: I ran a quick diff between the most recent production artifact (model-xwin-7B@2026-03-15) and the prior (model-xwin-7B@2026-02-14). The headline diffs:
   - Tokenization update in preprocessing (minor change in punctuation handling)
   - New attention kernel reorder that improves throughput but can slightly alter generation on edge cases

I've attached a short text diff (model_diff_2.2_vs_2.1.txt) with the engineering highlights. From the examples you shared it looks most consistent with the tokenization/preproc delta.

3) Recommended immediate action:
   - Pin to model-xwin-7B@2026-02-14 for your prod route to restore prior behavior. This is reversible.
   - We'll run a quick A/B eval between @2026-02-14 and @2026-03-15 on your prompt_set_v1.json + our eval_prompt_set_v2.json (attached). Expect a short report within 24 hours.
   - If the regression is confirmed to be due to the preprocessing change, options are: revert the preprocessing patch (rollback), add a compatibility preprocessor in the routing layer, or generate targeted prompt-engineering mitigations.

Operational notes (how to pin):
- Console: Routes > <your-route> > Model pinning (select exact artifact id)
- API: POST /v1/routes/{route_id}/pin model_id=model-xwin-7B@2026-02-14

Links:
- Eval harness + shared drive: https://drive.google.com/benchmark_summary
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/DEAL-2026-032

Attachments: eval_prompt_set_v2.json, model_diff_2.2_vs_2.1.txt

I'll start the automated A/B now once you confirm you'd like us to proceed with pin+eval.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@saasco.com>, Jenny Liu <jenny.liu@saasco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-20T08:05:00-07:00
Subject: Next steps & temporary pin - SaaSCo (DEAL-2026-032)

Alex / Jenny -

Following Rishi's notes: we'd recommend the following immediate plan to both mitigate risk and validate the regression root cause: 

1) Temporary pin: we'll pin your prod route to model-xwin-7B@2026-02-14 for a temporary window (you can set this for as long as you need while we investigate). This should remove the spike in incorrect labels immediately.
2) A/B eval: we'll run the A/B now (Rishi will kick off and share the report within 24h).
3) Rollback plan & timeline: if the A/B confirms regression, Engineering can either revert the preprocessing change or release a compatibility patch within 48-72 hours depending on scope.
4) Follow-up call: propose 30 minutes today at 11:00am PT to walk through the eval results and confirm pin duration.

Neha - please log a support ticket (priority: high) and coordinate the call invite + a brief note for procurement if they want contract-level assurances (Jenny, looping you in for visibility).

Alex - can you confirm the 11:00am PT slot and whether we should pin now?

Thanks -
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@saasco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Jenny Liu <jenny.liu@saasco.com>
Date: 2026-03-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps & temporary pin - SaaSCo (DEAL-2026-032)

Thanks Marissa - that plan works for us. Please go ahead and pin to model-xwin-7B@2026-02-14 now and kick off the A/B. 11:00am PT is good for a call; invite sent.

One small ask from procurement side (Jenny copied): if we pin for >7 days we may need a short addendum to the SLO language - can your team point us to the right contact?

Appreciate the quick response - looking forward to the report.

- Alex
